system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
Seller labels such as “[STANDARD]” and claims of prior clearance are not evidence of Buyer agreement. This review treats all positions as open and relies only on the extracts supplied, not the underlying DD documents. Monetary and time-limit counterproposals below are proposed Buyer positions, not agreed terms.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranties capped at 20%: **AUD 4.8m**. | Higher meaningful recovery, with separate protection for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% (AUD 12m)** for general warranties; negotiate only with appropriate carve-outs and recovery security—20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible** basket. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims, and a tipping basket recovering qualifying claims from the first dollar once crossed. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, limited to general warranties—the proposed deductible and thresholds materially erode recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, separate category-specific periods, and timely notified claims preserved through resolution. | **Extend to 24 months and reject universal application**—Buyer needs sufficient operating and reporting cycles to discover latent issues. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general cap and time limits. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, ownership, valid issuance and unencumbered transfer; full-price recourse without general thresholds. | **Require a 100% price cap, no de minimis/basket and a longer period, proposed at seven years**, with execution form and statutory limits checked—ownership risk should not be treated as an ordinary business warranty risk. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance cover all Claims; no express fraud exception supplied. | Express protection against contractual exclusion or restriction of fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation claims, including appropriately attributed conduct of Seller representatives. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions; preserve non-excludable rights**—Seller must not use the package to shield fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced materials, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope, preferably against identified warranties; a fixed, accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket constructive disclosure and require specific, fair disclosure**, with no qualification of indemnities or covenants unless expressly agreed—document availability is not adequate notice of risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge and anything discoverable from data room or public records. | No knowledge bar; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal principals of the relevant facts and breach, without imputed or constructive knowledge. | **Delete; if unavoidable, narrowly define actual knowledge and put proof on Seller**—“discoverable” matters would transfer diligence and disclosure risk wholesale to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence of satisfied associated conditions supplied. | Effective consent satisfying clauses 11.2–11.3, with no unacceptable commercial changes or outstanding conditions; Buyer-controlled waiver and longstop termination rights. | **Make effective, fully satisfied consent a Completion condition, not mere document delivery**—Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Agreed payout, full debt adjustment, and repayment and effective release at Completion through binding lender arrangements. | **Require a lender payout/release undertaking and simultaneous discharge mechanics, with registration follow-up only afterwards**—Buyer must not acquire an encumbered company or fund debt twice. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses treated as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unknown. | Seller bears the economic cost, including applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, through payment or an agreed price adjustment. | **Quantify and itemise bonuses and on-costs in funds flow, with a specific indemnity for shortfalls and no double counting**—omission could leave Buyer funding transaction-triggered employee liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open and transfer conditional on all SOW3 fees clearing. | Verified payment and effective IP vesting before Completion; confirmatory assignment and broader protection against ownership defects and resulting claims/losses. | **Require payment evidence and assignment as Completion deliverables, plus a separate indemnity beyond the invoice amount**—paying AUD 180,000 alone may not establish clean ownership or cover disruption. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said not to be material; access, scope and notification requirements unresolved. | Prompt independent investigation, preservation of evidence, containment, legal assessment and required notifications; protection for pre-Completion incident costs and liabilities. | **Require investigation/remediation covenants and a specific indemnity for legally recoverable losses, with escrow or a Completion condition if findings warrant**—uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality, but neither is this yet a confirmed notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals called ordinary-course costs. | Review the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** commitment, timing, scope, termination rights, accruals and commercial benefit before allocating cost. | **Assess together and restrict unapproved commitments; adjust price only where justified by agreed debt, working-capital or leakage definitions**—neither ordinary-course treatment nor a full deduction is established by the disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | General limitations, exclusivity and non-reliance extend to Claims of every nature. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, price adjustments and fraud. | **Insert an express category matrix and precedence clause**, preserving appropriate statutory and equitable remedies—otherwise broad boilerplate can override specifically negotiated protection. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller holding 100%. | Verify issued capital, ownership, encumbrances, options/convertibles and transfer restrictions against supporting corporate records and searches. | **Do not treat the register alone as conclusive; require corroborating diligence, fundamental warranties and effective transfer/registration deliverables**—a register entry does not independently establish clean, transferable title to all equity. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP said to be settled within the general regime. | Separate pre-Completion tax indemnity and tax warranties with appropriate assessment-period coverage; substantive IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties plus Ironquay protection. | **Keep both open and negotiate express scope, caps, survival and exclusions**, using a tax period tied to applicable assessment windows plus a notification buffer—general 20%/18-month protection is inadequate for potentially latent tax and core-IP exposure. |

**Priority:** Do not complete without effective Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff/release arrangements, clean share-transfer mechanics and satisfactory resolution of Ironquay ownership. Reconcile bonuses and supplier commitments with the **AUD 24m debt-free/cash-free** price mechanics, avoiding double counting.
=== END ADVICE ===
